headline: Eight US states have each sued OpenAI, saying ChatGPT harms children and that the company misled the public about how safe it is.
score_reason: Kept at pool score: fresh, several state governments, confirmed by multiple outlets.
importance_line: Eight state governments are now suing a leading AI company over child safety, which could force changes for young ChatGPT users and for OpenAI itself, though the claims are allegations that no court has tested.
summary: The Guardian reports that Iowa, Kansas, Nebraska, West Virginia, Arkansas, Arizona, Idaho and Montana filed separate suits in their own state courts, accusing OpenAI of breaking consumer protection laws and of building ChatGPT to be "overly agreeable"; OpenAI says it has built age-specific protections and will keep working with states. The states want changes to how the product works for young users, damages, and an order stopping OpenAI from developing self-improving models until it shows they match human values, and the Guardian calls it the first coordinated state action of this kind against an AI company.
notes: Reuters original (pool link) was blocked; read The Guardian instead, which reported on its own. Category LAW (courts, consumer protection).
